name: Vendor invoice exception handling redesign
description: Proposed reference scenario for replacing scattered accounts-payable exception handling with unified exception classification, ownership, deterministic three-way matching, and a read-only replay before any AI or payment-affecting change.
processNode: From receipt of a vendor invoice to the invoice becoming payment-eligible and entering the payment schedule; payment execution, vendor onboarding, and bank-detail changes are out of scope.
decisionOrAction: Decide whether the process owner reviews the proposed current-state assumptions and authorises a read-only replay over a de-identified batch of closed historical invoices; the replay does not write to the ERP or affect payment.

metrics.name: Receipt-to-payment-eligible time
metrics.definition: Median and high-percentile elapsed time from invoice receipt to payment eligibility.

metrics.name: First-pass match rate
metrics.definition: Share of invoices that complete three-way matching without entering the exception queue, with the distribution of exception types for the remainder.

metrics.name: Payment control incidents
metrics.definition: Count of erroneous releases, duplicate payments, and mispayments; the redesign must not increase this.
metrics.target: proposed:no worse than the accepted baseline

ontologyReferences.purpose: Proposed definitions for invoice case, exception type, reason code, responsible role, response deadline, escalation path, and payment eligibility.

sourceReferences.purpose: Current standard operating procedure, exception types, and responsibility split to be confirmed or corrected by the process owner.
Closed invoice cases from a representative recent period, used only for read-only replay after an access and de-identification decision.

acceptanceCriteria: The process owner accepts or corrects each step of the proposed current-state and target workflows.
The finance data owner confirms available fields, period, data quality, and usage rights for the historical cases.
Both owners approve the success conditions of a read-only replay that does not write back to the ERP or affect payment.
Deterministic three-way matching and duplicate-invoice checks are reproducible and keep prior results and a full audit trail when re-run after supplementation.
AI is considered only after replay evidence shows residual language work; it never approves payment, rewrites policy thresholds, changes vendor bank details, or releases exceptions.
notes: This record is proposed and generic. The real enterprise, process owner, current SOP, exception taxonomy, historical cases, baseline, target, and acceptance evidence are missing or unverifiable.
